admission.justification: One transaction test pins that an ordinary converted sync aligns through the same merge function, so a future route split that bypasses the alignment fails before it lands.

applicability: Crossing syncs and ordinary syncs of converted lines.
conditions: Both routes reach the shared merge through the same cross function.
exclusions: Input sides before conversion: cross() converts unconverted sides first and then calls the same merge_trees, so the shared operation governs the merge itself; this exclusion names the input phase, not the operation.

evidence: Rationale: both sync routes reach merge_trees through cross(), so the alignment, evidence and report behavior is one implementation, not two. Observed: test_an_ordinary_converted_sync_aligns_through_the_same_merge and the updated both-added integration test through the real worktree_sync transaction.

statement: Rule 9 every structural merge: crossing syncs and ordinary converted-line syncs share the same merge function
